description:
FILED s446i (Opus agent I), from the #513 probes.  The dup itself works now;
this is the residue.

REPRODUCERS (both through a PIPE, i.e. captured output):

    open(my $dup, ">&", \*STDOUT) or die;
    print $dup "via-dup\n";
    print "via-stdout\n";
    close $dup;
        perl  via-dup via-stdout      PCL  via-stdout via-dup

    open(my $dup, ">&", \*STDOUT) or die;
    print $dup "one\n"; print "two\n"; print $dup "three\n"; close $dup;
        perl  one three two           PCL  two one three

CAUSE, and it is NOT about dup: perl block-buffers a non-tty STDOUT, so
"via-stdout" sits in the buffer until exit while the dup's own buffer flushes
at `close $dup`.  PCL builds STDOUT with :buffering :line, so every plain print
leaves immediately, and the dup'd fd-stream takes SBCL's default (full)
buffering.  Matching perl means matching its buffering POLICY for the standard
handles (isatty-dependent), which is a global decision with its own sweep
price -- not a dup fix.

NOT a fix: making the dup'd stream line-buffered.  It makes the first
reproducer agree by coincidence (program order) and leaves the second wrong.

BAR (whenever this is taken): the two reproducers plus a tty run (where perl
line-buffers too and the orders agree), `$|=1` on either handle, and a dup of a
FILE handle (i6 in the s446i probes: both writes land, order irrelevant); the
io/ companion leg, because it is a runtime buffering change.


RULED s449 (Fable, 2026-08-29): APPROVED as its OWN session-sized change (never bundled) -- adopt perl-s buffering POLICY for the standard handles.  ONE policy function (rule 11) shared by boot construction (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:9488/9494) and every rebuild site (9718 and the #535 dup2 family): STDOUT line-buffered iff isatty(1), else :full; STDERR probe-and-match perl (unbuffered); a dup-d handle keeps its own buffer; $|/autoflush per handle keeps overriding.  REQUIRED: every normal exit path INCLUDING p-die->exit flushes the standard handles (perl flushes at exit even on die) -- otherwise block buffering turns a mid-file abort into invisible row loss (the LOST bucket).  NOT a fix: per-dup line buffering (task-s own warning).  Price accepted: full sweep + io/ companion leg with per-row explanations; any baseline rows that move on capture interleaving are edited by hand with cause.  Bar: the two reproducers + tty run + $|=1 + file-handle dup + a die-after-print flush probe.  Scheduled: Opus round 8.

DONE s451x (Opus agent X, 2026-08-29), two commits.

SHIPPED.  ONE policy function %p-output-buffering (fd) -- :line iff
isatty(fd), else :full -- plus %p-std-buffering's single exception, STDERR is
:none.  Asked by boot (a load-time call AND an *init-hooks* one, because the
isatty answer is PER PROCESS and a saved core would otherwise freeze the build
machine's), by %p-std-rebuild (every standard-handle re-point, the #535 dup2
family included), by %p-dup-make-stream, and by the fork-pipe parent's write
end.  The fork-pipe CHILD takes an override instead: perl's my_popen dup2s
under the same PerlIO handle, so the child keeps the PARENT's mode (probed --
a child of a pty parent line-buffers onto the pipe).  That call also replaced
an inline copy of the rebuild.

$| CARRY (the one thing the design did not name).  $| is the HANDLE's flag and
survives a reopen in perl (probed with an external observer); PCL keyed it on
the CL stream, which every rebuild replaces.  Pre-existing and invisible while
STDOUT was line-buffered -- with block buffering it cost t/io/dup.t its `ok 8`
(C_ok 10 -> 9) until %p-carry-autoflush was added to both re-point sites.

FLUSHES.  One helper %p-flush-all-output (std handles + the registered ones) at
every PERL_FLUSHALL_FOR_CHILD site: fork, fork-pipe, system, exec (BEFORE the
child -- it used to be after), backticks; and in the exit hook after the END
blocks.

THE EXIT PATH, MEASURED (SBCL 2.6.0), because the design's premise was wrong:
an unhandled error under --non-interactive DOES run sb-ext:*exit-hooks*, and
so does SIGTERM (what `timeout` sends the sweep's children).  Only
(sb-ext:exit ... :abort t) skips them, and PCL calls that in exactly two places
(p-exec, the fork-pipe exec failure) -- both now flush by hand.  So the die
path needs NO debugger hook.

DO NOT RETRY: a *invoke-debugger-hook* wrapper.  It was written and deleted.
(a) It is redundant given the above.  (b) It made the merged order WORSE:
flushing stdout inside the hook puts it BEFORE the diagnostic, where perl has
the diagnostic first.  (c) It cannot be installed from a saved core or from
sb-ext:*init-hooks* anyway -- `--non-interactive` becomes an ordered
(sb-ext:disable-debugger) in SBCL's option list and overwrites the hook
unconditionally (measured); only a call made after the options are processed
survives, i.e. from generated code.

BAR, all probed vs perl 5.40.3, through a PIPE and on a PTY (script -qec):
the task's two reproducers; $|=1; a dup of a FILE handle; STDOUT/STDERR
interleaving; print-then-system; dup-then-system; the fork-pipe child's
first-read latency; print-then-die (stdout and a file handle both survive);
plus three external-observer timing probes (STDERR partial line immediate /
STDOUT delayed; dup-of-STDERR block-buffered; $| survives a reopen).  All
identical after the change; the pipe leg had five DIFFs before it.

GUARD Pl/t/stdio-buffering-01.t, 9 rows, all pipe-observable, perl as oracle.
Inverse-checked against 718db6b's runtime: 6 of the 9 FAIL there.

MEASUREMENTS: gate 183/6149 PASS (xs skipped -- worktree).  companion io/ leg
(44 files): the only real mover is io/fflush.t 3/1 -> 4/0, its test 1 (flush on
fork/exec) -- a GAIN, snapshot row to be edited.  io/dup.t, io/pipe.t,
io/open.t, io/print.t, io/argv.t, io/tell.t all identical to the snapshot.
io/pvbm.t 23/5 and io/crlf_through.t 942/0 alone = snapshot (the known
contention flakes).  perl-tests named files (closure, die, die_exit, magic,
print) sum to exactly their pass-baseline rows.  cl/-only: NO generation bump.

RESIDUE FILED: #710 (a plain `open` onto a TERMINAL block-buffers -- cl:open
takes no :buffering, so the policy does not reach it), #711 (File::Temp shim:
tempfile(OPEN => 0) dies on a valid template).

TRAP worth remembering: a probe run immediately after a runtime edit measures
a CORE BUILD in its first case -- the $|-survives-reopen probe read DELAYED
once for that reason and IMMEDIATE on every warm re-run.
subject: Writes through a dup handle and through its source INTERLEAVE differently from perl -- PCL line-buffers STDOUT where perl block-buffers a non-tty, so `print $dup "a"; print "b"` comes out in the other order
